children.text: The Physics of a Microwave Oven

A model magnetron has a central cathode of radius a and a positive cylindrical anode of radius b, with eight LC resonator cavities. Adjacent cavities carry opposite oscillating charge. Their frequency is f=2.45 GHz. Static magnetic field B0 points out of the cross-section. The alternating electric-field amplitude is roughly one third of the static field, and electrons transfer about 80% of their acquired static-field energy to the oscillations. The resonator figure supplies its dimensions. Treat its slot as a parallel-plate capacitor and its cylindrical cavity as an inductor whose magnetic field is 0.6 times that of an infinite solenoid. Use ε0=8.85×10^−12 F/m, μ0=4π×10^−7 H/m, electron m=9.1×10^−31 kg, charge −e with e=1.6×10^−19 C, and c=3.0×10^8 m/s. For the operating magnetron use b−a=15 mm, B0=0.30 T and maximum kinetic energy 800 eV.

children.text: The Physics of a Microwave Oven
a.1. Cavity resonance estimate

If cavity radius is R, height h, slot length ℓ and width d, \(L=0.6\pi\mu_0R^2/h\), \(C=\epsilon_0\ell h/d\). Therefore \[f_{est}=\frac{c}{2\pi R}\sqrt{\frac d{0.6\pi\ell}}\simeq2.0\,\mathrm{GHz}.\] Height cancels. This approximate geometry need not reproduce 2.45 GHz exactly.
a.2. Crossed-field trajectories

\(\mathbf u_D=\mathbf E\times\mathbf B/B^2=-(E_0/B_0)\hat x\). Set ωc=eB0/m. If initial relative x velocity is vprime, then \[x(t)=-E_0t/B_0+(v^{\prime}/\omega_c)\sin\omega_ct,\quad y(t)=(v^{\prime}/\omega_c)(1-\cos\omega_ct).\] The two values are vprime=4E0/B0 and −2E0/B0, so radii are 4mE0/(eB0²) and 2mE0/(eB0²). Plot for 0<t<4π/ωc. Both have the same negative-x drift, with differently oriented loops.
a.3. Gyromotion radius bound

The relative circular speed is at most the laboratory maximum speed. Hence \(r\lesssim\sqrt{2mK_{max}}/(eB_0)=0.318\,\mathrm{mm}\). It is much smaller than the 15 mm gap, supporting the pure-drift approximation.
a.4. Radial drift directions

Use \(\mathbf u_D=\mathbf E\times\mathbf B/B^2\). Only the azimuthal electric field gives radial drift. A and B drift towards the cathode. C,D,E drift towards the anode. None of these five points is in the perpendicular-only category. The radial static field contributes only azimuthal drift.
a.5. Angular focusing

At equal radius the common static drift cancels from relative angular velocities. The radial alternating field focuses A,B,C and defocuses D,E,F. Thus AB,AC,BC decrease in angular separation, while DE,DF,EF increase.
a.6. Electron spokes

There are four spokes separated by π/2. They rotate counterclockwise. In one half-period the field flips and a spoke advances to the adjacent cavity, by π/4. Thus \(\omega_s=(\pi/4)/(1/2f)=\pi f/2=3.85\times10^9\,\mathrm{rad/s}\).
a.7. Operating voltage
At r=(a+b)/2 the drift speed V0/[B0(b−a)] equals rωs. Hence \[V_0=\frac{\pi fB_0}{4}(b^2-a^2).\] This is a model estimate of the minimum operating voltage.
b.1. Dipole torque and work

The restoring signed torque is \(\tau_z=-p_0E(t)\sin\theta\), so its magnitude is \(|p_0E\sin\theta|\). Power is \(H_i=\tau_z\dot\theta=-p_0E\sin\theta\dot\theta=E\,d(p_0\cos\theta)/dt\). Torque magnitude alone must not be used for signed work.
b.2. Mean dielectric heating
Power density is \(H=E\dot P\). Averaging the product of sine and phase-shifted cosine gives \[\langle H\rangle=\tfrac12\beta\epsilon_0\omega E_0^2\sin\delta.\]
b.3. Attenuation with depth

Total mean energy density is εrε0E0(z)²/2, so \(I=\sqrt{\epsilon_r}\epsilon_0cE_0(z)^2/2\). Energy balance gives \(dI/dz=-\langle H\rangle=-\beta\omega\sin\delta\,I/(c\sqrt{\epsilon_r})\). Thus \[I(z)=I(0)\exp[-\beta\omega z\sin\delta/(c\sqrt{\epsilon_r})].\]
b.4. Polarization coefficient
Squaring the field gives intensity attenuation exponent \(-\sqrt{\epsilon_r}\omega z\tan\delta/c\). Match this with B3 to obtain β=εr in the stated approximation.
b.5. Penetration depth and temperature

At 20°C read εr≈78 and εloss≈10. Then \[z_{1/2}=\frac{c\sqrt{\epsilon_r}\ln2}{\omega\epsilon_{loss}}\simeq12\,\mathrm{mm}.\] In pure water εloss decreases strongly on warming, so penetration increases. In dilute salt solution εloss increases while εr decreases, so penetration decreases. These are trends at the fixed specified frequency, not all frequencies.
